sections.html:
Appleton is the Outagamie County seat, a Fox River city of 75,452 people (July 2025 estimate), about 30 miles southwest of Green Bay and 100 miles north of Milwaukee. Most of the city lies in Outagamie County, with small pieces in Calumet and Winnebago counties, and that detail decides which county treasurer and Register of Deeds you deal with. Check which county your parcel is in early.

Several neighboring communities, including the Town of Grand Chute and the Village of Harrison, carry an Appleton mailing address without being inside the city. Building Inspections advises confirming a property is within city limits before buying a permit.

About two-thirds of Appleton homes are owner-occupied, and the median owner-occupied home is valued at $231,400. These are the numbers a buyer's agent will start from.

sections.h2: Permits and repairs before you sell
sections.html:
Getting a house ready may require a permit. Building Inspections says decks, remodeling, pools, siding and sheds over 50 square feet most likely do. If you are not sure, call (920) 832-6411 before you start. In-office hours at City Hall are 8:00 a.m. to 9:30 a.m. on weekdays.

A homeowner can pull permits for a single-family home they own and live in, under the same rules a contractor follows. Residential contractors must be registered with the State, and the city suggests asking for the registration number. If an inspection is never finished, the permit stays open and a re-inspection fee can follow.

An inherited house that has been neglected may draw the city's attention: after a complaint it can cut grass and clear debris, and may need inspection warrants to do it. A free courtesy inspection from Building Inspections lists what would bring a building into compliance.

Setbacks vary by zoning. Side setbacks are 8 feet in R-1A and 6 feet in R-1B, and the rear setback is 25 feet in R-1A, R-1B, R-1C and R-2. Check them before you promise a buyer a garage or an addition.

sections.h2: The assessor and a sold house
sections.html:
Each fall and winter the Assessor's Office inspects homes that recently sold, so expect a letter about your sale, with online scheduling offered. The office also checks houses with building permits and scans online listings for work done without one. The assessor's number is (920) 832-5850.

All property is revalued at least once every five years, and the aim is to inspect each parcel at least once in ten. For formal objections, the spring schedule has notices mailed in April, an open book period, then a Board of Review in late April. Ask the assessor each spring for the new dates, and call the City Clerk's Office at (920) 832-6443 to file.

One point surprises owners: when the bill lands in December it is too late to object, and paying under protest counts only if you first filed with the Board of Review.

Appleton offers four installments, due January 31, March 31, May 31 and July 31. A late payment cancels the installment option and adds monthly interest on the unpaid balance, as state law requires. After the last installment, outstanding balances are delinquent and move to the county treasurer for the county where the parcel sits.

  • In person: City Hall, 100 N. Appleton St., weekdays 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., or the night deposit box.
  • By mail: City of Appleton, P.O. Box 2519, Appleton, WI 54912-2519.
  • Online: card or e-check, using the parcel number. The payment vendor charges a convenience fee that the city does not receive.
  • Delinquent bills: Outagamie County at (920) 832-5065, Calumet County at (920) 849-1457 or Winnebago County at (920) 232-3420.

Before closing, ask the City Finance Department at (920) 832-6442 for the paid-to-date figure and pass it to the title company. Refunds over $750, and any refund for a payment made by mail or drop box, take four to six weeks to arrive.

Fill out the Wisconsin Real Estate Transfer Return on the Department of Revenue website, print the receipt, and bring it to the Register of Deeds with the deed and fees. A completed return and fee collection come before recording (s. 77.22(1)). Most of Appleton falls under the Outagamie County Register of Deeds. A parcel in the Calumet or Winnebago portion is recorded in that county.

Outagamie charges $30 for a standard real estate document and stops recording at 4:00 p.m. Each document needs a blank 3 inch by 3 inch space in the upper right corner, a parcel number, a full legal description, notarized signatures and the drafter's name.

Wisconsin also expects sellers of one to four unit homes to give the buyer a real estate condition report within 10 days after the offer is accepted. If it is late, the buyer may rescind under s. 709.02. If the house took storm damage, say so on the report and keep insurance and repair records together.

sections.h2: Can I rent out my Appleton house before it sells?
sections.html:
Any stay shorter than a month counts as a short-term rental, and the city treats it as a tourist rooming house under the Health Department. You need the license before offering a stay, plus a pre-inspection and an annual health inspection. Licenses renew on July 1 and expire June 30. Call the Health Department at 920-832-6429.

Hosts who rent on their own must register with the Department of Revenue and collect state and county sales tax once total sales revenue reaches $2,000, and they must collect local room tax.

There are three routes: list with an agent, sell it yourself, or take a cash offer. A listing reaches the most buyers but depends on showings, inspections and the condition report. Selling alone saves a commission and leaves the contract, disclosure and paperwork to you. A cash buyer can close sooner and buy the house as is, which fits inherited homes, tenants in place or repairs you cannot afford.

Whichever route you choose, line up the same four items: a paid-to-date tax figure from Finance, a permit history from Building Inspections, the condition report, and the transfer return. Having them early keeps the closing date from slipping.

faqs.q: How fast can I sell my house in Appleton, WI?
faqs.a: It depends on the route and on how soon the title, tax balance and condition report are ready. A listing adds time for showings and the buyer's financing, and a one to four unit home needs the condition report within 10 days after the offer is accepted.

faqs.q: Who do I pay Appleton property taxes to?
faqs.a: The City of Appleton Finance Department takes payments through the final installment on July 31. After that, balances are delinquent and go to the treasurer of Outagamie, Calumet or Winnebago County, depending on the parcel.

faqs.q: Does Appleton require an inspection before I sell?
faqs.a: No inspection is required to sell. Work you do first, such as decks, siding, remodeling and sheds over 50 square feet, may need a permit. Call Building Inspections at (920) 832-6411 if you are unsure.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Appleton?
faqs.a: The Outagamie County Register of Deeds charges $30 for a standard real estate document. You also file a Real Estate Transfer Return with the Department of Revenue, and any transfer fee is paid when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Can I list my Appleton house as a vacation rental?
faqs.a: Yes, with a Tourist Rooming House license from the Appleton Health Department. A pre-inspection is required and licenses renew each July 1. Call 920-832-6429 to schedule it.
